editorial:
Imagine having a mother who loves you so much that she actually ruins your life just to keep you close. That is exactly what happens in this old-school drama. You follow a young man from Arkansas who just wants to start his own life and get married. But his mother is way too possessive. She is so scared of losing him to another woman that she does something truly wild: she helps get him drafted into World War I. It is a strange and tense setup that feels more like a family fight than a typical war movie, making the whole experience feel personal and heavy.

What really hits home is the acting and the way the story builds up its emotion. While the pacing is a bit slower than modern films, the tension between the son and his mother is great. You will probably find the mother's actions shocking, which is exactly what the movie wants. If you are into classic cinema, you should definitely try renting this on Apple TV or adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection for the best quality. It is a great pick for anyone who loves stories about family secrets and the cost of love.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when the son survives the war and returns home. The mother finally has to face the guilt of what she did to her own child. You see a shift in her character as she realizes that her love was actually selfish and hurtful. The movie wraps up with a feeling of sadness and forgiveness, showing that while the family is broken, they can finally find some peace and move forward.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic family dramas and historical war stories.
